title: Thursday, September 3, 2026

headline.title: Five more companies beat last night and four of them are being sold. What the market is paying for is the guide, not the quarter. AVGO −3.4% beat on both lines and guided Q4 revenue to $34.8B against $35.03B — and Q4 non-GAAP operating margin to 66% against 66.5%. NTAP −9.4% beat by $0.46, guided above, raised the full year, and printed gross margin 70.6% vs 69.7% expected — then lost nine percent on deferred revenue of $4.85B against $4.86B. HPE −5.1% beat by $0.18 and guided FY27 earnings growth to 16-20% against 18.7% consensus. SNOW +23.4% is the exception, and the reason is precise.
headline.summary: SNOW cut its product gross margin guide by 100 basis points and gained 23%. AVGO cut its Q4 operating margin guide by 50 basis points and lost 3%. The difference is which line: SNOW raised FY27 operating margin guidance to 14.5% from 13.5% and let gross margin go on AI mix. The market is paying for operating leverage and forgiving the cost of getting it. AVGO also got upgraded to Outperform at Macquarie with a $490 target this morning and is still down 3% — a 50bp forward margin miss outweighed an upgrade.

overview: The index split three ways yesterday and only one of them has a trigger today. SPY printed a 2 Up closing 765.16 near its high, IWM printed a 2 Up closing 294.01 exactly at its high — its first up day after three straight 2 Downs — and QQQ went inside, no trigger, and is still inside this morning at 707.91. Breadth is leading and the Nasdaq is coiled, with the 10-year down 3bps to 4.77% underneath it. That coil resolves into ISM Services at 9:00am CT, thirty minutes after the open. Underneath, the guide-not-the-quarter rule is doing all the work: SNOW +23.4% dragged the whole software complex up with it (DDOG +5.9%, NOW +3.1%, NET +2.2%) after those same names sat in yesterday's bleed bucket. Energy is bid without a headline — WTI +2.2% to $93.01 and Brent pushing $100 on the Hormuz escalation, while Trump has zero on-camera events today and Reuters reports his advisors are pushing him to keep Iran quiet into the midterms. An oil bid with no one talking is positioning, not news. And TSLA launches Cybercab in Austin today, +1.6% premarket, the biggest mover on the Mag 11 board.

Over 709.80 is the 1-2 up, under 705.10 is the 1-2 down, and the thing most likely to pick is ISM Services at 9:00am CT, thirty minutes after the open. Trading the coil before the data is paying for someone else's decision.

The cleanest structure on the index board and the one nobody is looking at. IWM printed 2 Downs on 8/28, 8/31 and 9/1, then Wednesday took 292.94 and closed 294.01 at its 294.35 high — a 2 Up that finished on its high after three days of lower highs and lower lows. The 10-year at 4.77%, down 3bps, is the tailwind. Premarket flat, so the reversal has not been given back.

The sharpest test of the rule on the board. NTAP beat by $0.46, guided Q2 above, raised FY27, and printed non-GAAP gross margin 70.6% against 69.7% expected — a margin beat. It is down nine percent on deferred revenue of $4.85B against $4.86B, a $10M miss on the forward-bookings line. Wednesday was already a Failed 2U (took 185.30 to 189.21, closed 180.77 back below); premarket 163.78 is far under Wednesday's 180.03 low. Trailing margin did not save it. The forward number decided it.

WTI +2.2% to $93.01, Brent pushing $100. The U.S. escorted 40 commercial vessels carrying 18 million barrels through the Strait of Hormuz Tuesday and expects to continue offensive strikes near the waterway; Kuwait's army confronted Iranian missile and drone attacks. Gold is moving with it: futures +1.7% to $4,487.40, GDX +1.9%.

SNOW is the momentum name, RBLX is the swing, AVGO is the breakdown, and TSLA has a launch with no announced time. The index has one trigger (IWM), one coil (QQQ), and ISM Services at 9:00am CT sitting thirty minutes into the session.

Contract selection from the sweep: 9/18 42.5C / 45C, 9/25 43C / 45C. Both legs sit past RDC26 on purpose — a 9/11 weekly would expire on day two of the conference and never see the follow-through. Added to the catalyst calendar.

tts.label: Premarket
tts.text: Thursday September third, premarket. Five more companies beat last night and four of them are being sold. What the market is paying for is the guide, not the quarter. Broadcom beat on both lines and is down three and a half percent, because it guided fourth quarter revenue to thirty four point eight billion against thirty five point zero three, and fourth quarter operating margin to sixty six percent against sixty six and a half. NetApp beat by forty six cents, guided above, raised the full year, and beat on gross margin at seventy point six against sixty nine point seven, and it is down nine percent on a ten million dollar miss in deferred revenue. Hewlett Packard Enterprise beat by eighteen cents and is down five, on fiscal twenty seven earnings growth guidance of sixteen to twenty percent against eighteen point seven expected. Snowflake is the exception, up twenty three percent, and the reason is precise. Snowflake cut its gross margin guide by a hundred basis points and gained twenty three percent. Broadcom cut its operating margin guide by fifty basis points and lost three. The market is paying for operating leverage and forgiving the cost of getting it.

tts.label: Movers
tts.text: Snowflake up twenty three point four, and it is pulling the whole software complex with it. Datadog up five point nine, ServiceNow up three point one, Cloudflare up two point two, Salesforce up one point six. Those same names sat in yesterday's A I adjacent bleed bucket. On the other side, NetApp down nine point four, Campbell's down six and a half after cutting its dividend thirty six percent, Hewlett Packard Enterprise down five point one, Broadcom down three point four. Ultragenyx is down forty six and a half percent after its Phase three Angelman trial missed both its primary and key secondary endpoints, and it has taken four downgrades this morning. Energy is bid across the board with W T I up two point two percent to ninety three dollars and one cent, and gold futures up one point seven to forty four eighty seven.
